record.paper_title: Measurement of Energy Spectrum and Elemental Composition of PeV Cosmic Rays: Open Problems and Prospects
record.original_question: If the knee and related spectral features follow a rigidity-dependent pattern, are they caused primarily by maximum acceleration energy at cosmic-ray sources or by inefficient Galactic confinement and escape, and what measurements of proton and other mass-group spectra up to about 10^17 eV can decide between these rigidity-acceleration and rigidity-confinement interpretations?

evidence.quote: The observed features in the all-particle energy spectrum seem to be consistent with the bending of different components in a rigidity-based scenario. However, rigidity models can be • rigidity-acceleration models, that is, the knee can be an acceleration feature, a source property, related to the maximum energy of particle acceleration inside the CR sources; • rigidity-confinement models, that is, the knee is related to inefficient confinement of particles in the galaxy. In this case, the galaxy could contain ’super-PeVatrons’, astrophysical objects able to accelerate particles well beyond the PeV.

In the coming years, the LHAASO experiment is expected to be able to measure the energy spectra of different mass groups up to 1017 eV and to determine the energy of the proton knee, thus clarifying the origin of the knee in the all-particle spectrum.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Cosmic rays arriving at Earth exhibit an all-particle differential energy spectrum that follows an approximate power law in kinetic energy E but features a steepening, called the "knee," near a few PeV (1 PeV = 10^15 eV). Two broad classes of rigidity-dependent models are proposed for this feature and its high-energy continuation. Here a particle of charge Z has magnetic rigidity R = E/Z, and a "rigidity model" predicts that each elemental mass group i with charge Z_i has a spectrum φ_i(E) whose characteristic spectral break occurs at an energy E_i = Z_i · R_0 for a common rigidity R_0.

(A) Rigidity-acceleration models: the break at rigidity R_0 reflects the maximum rigidity to which Galactic sources can accelerate cosmic rays, so the spectrum of each species exhibits an intrinsic cutoff at E_i = Z_i R_0 imprinted at the source.

(B) Rigidity-confinement models: sources can accelerate particles to rigidities well above R_0 ("super-PeVatron" sources), but Galactic magnetic confinement becomes inefficient above R_0, so the diffusion coefficient D(R) steepens above R_0 and the propagated spectrum of each species softens at E_i = Z_i R_0.

Problem. Working within this two-class framework, determine:
(i) whether the observed knee and the spectral features extending up to about 10^17 eV in the all-particle cosmic-ray spectrum are produced primarily by mechanism (A) or by mechanism (B); and
(ii) which quantitative measurements of the individual mass-group energy spectra φ_i(E) — in particular the proton (Z = 1) spectrum and the spectra of heavier mass groups up to roughly 10^17 eV, including the energy and shape of the proton knee, the dependence of the break energies on Z, and the high-energy behavior beyond the break — suffice to discriminate between (A) and (B).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent LHAASO measurements (2024–2025) have precisely identified the cosmic-ray proton component and measured its spectrum from ~0.15 to 12 PeV, locating a sharp proton softening around 3 PeV that aligns with the all-particle knee at ~3.67 PeV. Subsequent analyses (e.g., joint spectrum-and-anisotropy studies, and a 2025 result linking the knee to micro-quasar accelerators) increasingly favor an acceleration-limit (source) interpretation of the knee, with a new high-energy component emerging at PeV energies. The discrimination program is in progress: key proton-knee measurements have been made, but mass-group spectra up to 10^17 eV are not yet fully resolved, so the question is partially solved rather than settled.

status_evidence.title: First Identification and Precise Spectral Measurement of the Proton Component in the Cosmic-Ray 'Knee'
status_evidence.snippet: LHAASO reports high-purity identification of cosmic-ray protons and precise measurement of the proton energy spectrum from 0.15 to 12 PeV, with hardening culminating at ~3 PeV followed by sharp softening aligned with the all-particle knee.
status_evidence.claim: Proton-spectrum measurements relevant to discriminating the knee origin have been performed.

status_evidence.title: LHAASO Uncovers Mystery of Cosmic Ray 'Knee' Formation (CAS)
status_evidence.snippet: The knee is interpreted as an acceleration limit of Galactic sources, with new sources such as micro-quasars proposed as PeV accelerators.
status_evidence.claim: Recent results favor an acceleration-limit interpretation of the knee.

status_evidence.title: Joint constraint on the propagation origin of the cosmic-ray spectral knee
status_evidence.snippet: Combined energy-spectrum and anisotropy observations are used to constrain whether the knee originates from propagation/confinement effects.
status_evidence.claim: Confinement-origin scenarios remain under active quantitative testing.
